drivingQuestion: Why is entering the field forbidden in the Sabbatical Year when the land is also rendered ownerless?
outcomeNote: the difficulty is answered in the next unit (nedarim.sugya129)

segments.he: וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית אֵין יוֹרֵד לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ כּוּ׳. מַאי שְׁנָא דְּאוֹכֵל מִן הַנּוֹטוֹת — דְּפֵירֵי דְהֶפְקֵירָא אִינּוּן, אַרְעָא נָמֵי אַפְקְרַהּ?!
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «And during the Sabbatical Year he may not enter his field;» however, he eats from the produce that leans out of the field. The Gemara asks: «What is different» about the Sabbatical Year «that he» is permitted to «eat of» the produce that leans out of the field? It is «due to» the fact «that the produce is ownerless.» With regard to «land as well,» the Torah «rendered it ownerless,» as during the Sabbatical Year, it is permitted for everyone to enter the field and eat the produce.

moves.about: lemma on not entering the field in the Sabbatical Year
